name: Build usable sentences
phonology: Word boundaries, stressed syllables, clear final consonants and meaningful pauses
reading: Find explicitly stated people, actions, objects and locations in short texts.
listening: Recognise familiar words and retrieve a stated item, number or place without relying on the transcript.
speaking: Give an intelligible personal answer using two linked statements.
writing: Write complete SVO sentences with clear reference and basic punctuation.
scaffolding: Brief optional first-language explanation, illustrated meaning, model sentence and replay in learning mode; remove them for the final retrieval.
exam_focus: Understand the four skill names; distinguish an answer from an explanation; type exact words. Do not impose full-test timing.
gate: Demonstrate short-text comprehension and independent simple production; early band labels are curriculum orientation, not a scored IELTS conversion.

name: Manage everyday exchanges
phonology: Plural endings, contracted forms, weak function words and question intonation
reading: Follow instructions, locate quantities and distinguish routines from current actions.
listening: Complete a simple form from a two-speaker exchange and track a correction.
speaking: Ask and answer practical questions with a relevant follow-up.
writing: Link accurate simple sentences into a short functional paragraph.
scaffolding: One worked example per new operation; optional replay before a fresh no-transcript attempt.
exam_focus: Word limits, numbers, singular/plural answers and the mechanics of form completion.
gate: Complete unseen everyday tasks without copying a model; retain earlier sentence patterns across changed topics.

name: Narrate, compare and explain
phonology: Regular past endings, irregular verb recognition and phrase-level stress
reading: Identify chronology, compare options and support a literal answer with a precise text span.
listening: Follow a sequence and distinguish an initial suggestion from the final decision.
speaking: Tell a short past experience, compare two choices and explain a preference.
writing: Produce a coherent paragraph with a main idea, reason and example.
scaffolding: Keyword notes rather than full scripts; gradually remove sentence starters.
exam_focus: Short answers, simple multiple choice, sentence completion and Speaking Part 1 development.
gate: Control past/present reference and give relevant reasons in unfamiliar everyday contexts.

name: Connect ideas and follow arguments
phonology: Linking, contrastive stress, prominent content words and self-monitoring of intelligibility
reading: Track reference and cause; distinguish explicit contradiction from missing information.
listening: Identify key details, speaker intentions and changes of plan in short sustained audio.
speaking: Describe and explain with a clear beginning, development and conclusion.
writing: Organise two connected paragraphs; begin describing data and reporting a process.
scaffolding: Teach the question mechanics on a different text; progressively delay feedback until task submission.
exam_focus: True/False/Not Given, matching information, maps, basic Academic Task 1 and Part 2 planning.
gate: Preserve the source meaning, complete coherent tasks and distinguish knowledge gaps from careless answer-format errors.

name: Enter sustained IELTS-style tasks
phonology: Multiword chunks, reduced forms, emphasis and intelligible multi-clause delivery
reading: Identify paragraph purpose, paraphrase and supporting detail without searching for exact word repetition.
listening: Follow everyday and study-related exchanges across a complete question block.
speaking: Sustain a relevant long turn and justify a straightforward opinion.
writing: Write an overview from data and develop a position in a short argument.
scaffolding: Planning frames optional during learning only; guided tasks and fresh timed tasks use different facts.
exam_focus: Matching headings, table/flow completion, Task 1 overview and Task 2 question analysis.
gate: Attempt complete IELTS-style task shapes with explicit gap diagnosis rather than inflated projected bands.

name: Build independent four-skill performance
phonology: Natural pacing, clause boundaries, correction without repeated restarting and accent variation
reading: Summarise relationships between claims, evidence and examples in extended prose.
listening: Follow educational discussion and a short lecture with reduced replay support.
speaking: Develop Part 2 fully and answer explanatory Part 3 questions spontaneously.
writing: Produce complete Task 1 and Task 2 responses, initially with separate untimed revision.
scaffolding: Task plan rather than language template; gradual transition to 20/40-minute writing budgets.
exam_focus: All major task families encountered; introduce complete section attempts and self-analysis.
gate: Produce sustained independent work in all four skills; keep skill scores separate.

name: Control complex meaning
phonology: Prosodic grouping, contrast, unobtrusive self-repair and intelligibility during extended explanations
reading: Track scope, qualification, author stance and similarities across paraphrases.
listening: Track agreement, disagreement and attributed opinions in educational discussions.
speaking: Explain causes, alternatives and hypothetical consequences with relevant development.
writing: Maintain a clear position and accurate comparisons; correct recurring cohesion and grammar problems.
scaffolding: No lexical preteaching for scored holdouts; diagnose after submission and repair on parallel materials.
exam_focus: Yes/No/Not Given, features, multiple selection and precise Task 1 comparisons.
gate: Show repeatable transfer beyond rehearsed topics and reduce persistent error families.

name: Develop flexible academic performance
phonology: Flexible emphasis and phrasing; recognise unfamiliar voices without assuming a single preferred accent
reading: Distinguish claims from evidence and interpret implication without importing outside knowledge.
listening: Follow extended argument and retain the final position after concessions and corrections.
speaking: Handle abstract follow-ups, challenge an assumption politely and reformulate clearly.
writing: Develop evidence-led arguments and logically group major features in Task 1.
scaffolding: Support follows the learner's documented error pattern; full mocks have none.
exam_focus: Integrated timing, passage triage, precise claim matching and complete analytic writing criteria.
gate: Meet intermediate-high readiness criteria on fresh forms; no weak skill can be hidden by a high overall average.

name: Handle nuance and unfamiliarity
phonology: Meaningful intonation, listener-friendly pace and adaptation to unfamiliar speakers
reading: Resolve ambiguity, trace alternative explanations and avoid overgeneralising a qualified statement.
listening: Infer attitude from wording and prosody while preserving what is explicitly versus implicitly supported.
speaking: Discuss unfamiliar issues, qualify conclusions and develop a reasoned counterargument.
writing: Build precise, relevant arguments with adequate development and measured claims.
scaffolding: Targeted micro-repair between complete performances, not hints inside an assessment.
exam_focus: Difficult distractors, scope changes, mixed datasets, counterarguments and unfamiliar Part 3 topics.
gate: Sustain accuracy under realistic time pressure across multiple domains and speakers.

name: Prioritise precision and control
phonology: Consistent intelligibility, flexible stress and smooth spontaneous reformulation
reading: Interpret dense prose, distinguish methodological limits and verify each inference against evidence.
listening: Track layered positions, implicit qualification and lecture organisation with one examination playback.
speaking: Use precise, natural language rather than forced idioms; respond directly and flexibly.
writing: Select the strongest relevant support and maintain control of complete timed responses.
scaffolding: Models shown only after the independent attempt; blind compare and justify revisions.
exam_focus: Full-length form practice, rater-anchored comparisons and recurring small-error elimination.
gate: High performance must persist on unseen tasks; a model answer imitation is not evidence of independent ability.

name: Refine expert-level communication
phonology: Stable connected speech, unobtrusive repair, precise focus and effortless listener comprehension
reading: Resolve fine distinctions, evaluate competing interpretations and retain exact scope under time pressure.
listening: Recognise shifts in stance and rapidly recover after a missed detail without losing the next answer.
speaking: Give fully developed spontaneous responses and negotiate nuanced follow-ups coherently.
writing: Produce well-developed, appropriately qualified arguments with very high lexical and grammatical control.
scaffolding: Only pre-task logistics; all language support is outside sealed performance episodes.
exam_focus: Plateau diagnostics, fresh parallel tasks, scoring disagreement audits and complete mock series.
gate: Separate occasional unsystematic slips from persistent limitations; verify through independent calibrated assessment.

name: Demonstrate robust band-9-target readiness
orientation: 8.5 towards 9 demands; not a promised score
phonology: Natural, flexible, intelligible speech whose accent does not obstruct understanding
reading: Achieve near-complete supported comprehension on varied unseen passages and all question families.
listening: Achieve near-complete comprehension on varied unseen natural recordings and all question families.
speaking: Demonstrate the complete high-band analytic profile in fresh, interactive interviews.
writing: Demonstrate the complete high-band analytic profile on unfamiliar timed Task 1 and Task 2 prompts.
scaffolding: None in readiness assessments. Repair tasks remain available after submission and do not overwrite scores.
exam_focus: Sealed mixed-topic mock forms, calibrated productive assessment, retention and transfer checks.
gate: A conditional readiness decision requires multiple independent fresh performances and valid scoring. An actual IELTS result remains the examination outcome.
